title: Existing projective curve branch, multiplicity and tangent data
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $r\in\mathbf N$, and $D$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Put $A=\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ using $r$ homogeneous coordinates [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. For a reduced irreducible component $Z$ of $D$, let $C_Z$ be its function-field normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization, def-sc-normalization] and $
u_Z:C_Z	o D$ the canonical composite [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]. A branch above $p\in D$ is a pair $(Z,q)$ with $q\in C_Z$ and $
u_Z(q)=p$, retaining its component label. Its local map is the stalk map $\mathcal O_{D,p}	o\mathcal O_{C_Z,q}$, transported along this equality of points; its branch ideal is the image of $\mathfrak m_p$ under this map. For a morphism $i:D	o A$, the component degree is the degree of $(i
u_Z)^*\mathcal O_A(1)$ with its induced $k$-structure [def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. The predicate $\mathrm{HasMultiplicity}(D,p,t)$, for $t\in\mathbf N$, means that there exist $a\in\mathbf Z$ and $N\in\mathbf N$ such that for every $n\ge N$ the length of $\mathcal O_{D,p}/\mathfrak m_p^{n+1}$ is finite and equals $tn+a$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. The tangent image of a branch is the image in $T_{A/k,i(p)}$ of the tangent map of $i
u_Z$, using the canonical induced residue-field isomorphism whenever that map is bijective, and transporting its point index along $
u_Z(q)=p$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. For a coefficient vector $a=(a_m)$ and a coordinate $x_j$ nonvanishing at $x\in A$, its linear germ is the germ of $\sum_m a_m x_m/x_j$ with the structural $k$-map. The line equations are coefficient vectors whose linear germ pulls back to zero along every tangent vector in this branch image, in every such coordinate frame, with the closed-point stalk transport. Order at least two means that the pullback of each linear germ to the branch local ring lies in $\mathfrak m_q^2$; this includes the zero germ. Finally the split-node completion predicate at $p$ means the existence of a ring isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D,p}\simeq k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ preserving the structural $k$-map [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. These are definitions only: no branch multiplicity, degree, tangent or node criterion is asserted. The constructions use [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], [def-sc-normalization], [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve], [def-pc-projective-space-twist], [def-pc-module-pullback], [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], [def-weil-pbc-module-length], [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

from.place: Definitions of normalization branches, local multiplicity and tangent equations used to state the singular-point jet estimates. det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images, proof (3), alteration reduction through ILO X Lemma 2.2: dimension induction in the marked plurinodal input; one relative curve, de Jong Theorem 2.4, Lemmas 5.5 and 5.7, before induction on its base; replacement prerequisite: de Jong Lemma 3.7, printed p.608, including the prime-to-characteristic level-structure choice which makes the base alteration generically etale; §3.6 supplies the smooth genus-at-least-two input. Moduli prerequisite: projective compactification with prime-to-characteristic level structure and its universal stable family, used before taking the closure of a generic lift. Projectivity of the unpointed stable coarse moduli scheme. Supporting input: Gieseker stability and closedness of the ten-canonical locus. This input serves Section 3.2, Definition 7 and Theorem 8, printed pp.13--15, and equation (6) in Section 3.3. Local PDF WANTED; read online.
